title: NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games - CBS Sports
description: NFL teams might have to change the way they travel for international games
body:
NFL teams might have to change the way they travel for international games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:28 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.The NFL is currently exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic, NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming."Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."It's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams. The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture. 
On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off. The Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the plan backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss. If the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday. 
That exact travel plan was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers, Texans, Colts, and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a new travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change. Since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss. There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a new travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route). 
Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a new travel policy is in place for next season.

title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs laying early foundation for one of the best running back careers ever - CBS Sports
description: Gibbs is only 3.5 years into his NFL career, and he's on a few different record-breaking paces
body:
Gibbs is only 3.5 years into his NFL career, and he's on a few different record-breaking paces
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:30 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery. Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards. Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season. All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995). 
Most games with 150-plus rush yards and a rush TD, First 9 games of a season all-timeMost such games Jim Brown (1958)5Jahmyr Gibbs (2026)4Emmitt Smith (1995)4O.J. Simpson (1975)4O.J. Simpson (1974)4Jim Brown (1963)4Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff, a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver (Amon-Ra St. Brown), a Pro Bowl tight end (Sam LaPorta), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle (Penei Sewell), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver (Jameson Williams). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season. Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine. Here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.

Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.

title: Damian Lillard stars in his Milwaukee return in another stark reminder of how bleak things are for the Bucks - CBS Sports
description: In his first game back in Milwaukee, Lillard led Portland to a win over the hapless -- and hopeless -- Bucks
body:
In his first game back in Milwaukee, Lillard led Portland to a win over the hapless -- and hopeless -- Bucks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:30 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory. Bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record. Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery. Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he said, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt." 
Lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard said. 
No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range. "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori said pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it."
The moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then. The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season. "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard said Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on."
The desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury. 
        
            
                Re-grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade: Why the Heat and Bucks both look much worse now
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference. And the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract. 
No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks. Just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

title: Anxiety Rankings: Can Tennessee avoid nightmare in Neyland? Big 12 living on the edge - CBS Sports
description: It's both business and personal Saturday for the Volunteers when Lane Kiffin comes to town intent on taking away
body:
It's both business and personal Saturday for the Volunteers when Lane Kiffin comes to town intent on taking away their playoff hopes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:46 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There are very few things in life that can stir emotions within you like college football. For four months a year, millions of Americans decide to put their mental well-being in the hands of a collection of 18- to 24-year-old men they do not know personally. All they know is that they've chosen to wear their preferred uniform. Sometimes this decision brings joy. Other times it brings pain.But what it always brings as kickoff draws near every week is anxiety. There's always the nervous energy of the unknown heading into a game. You can never be sure how things will go, and where the rollercoaster will take you. However, while we all feel it, some of us feel it more than others, and each week, The Anxiety Rankings aim to find the five most anxious places in the country.Welcome to Week 12. The end is approaching. Try to stay calm. You'll fail, but try all the same.1. The Big 12Here's the good news: When the College Football Playoff selection committee released its latest rankings on Tuesday, there were two Big 12 teams currently in the field (No. 2 Utah and No. 10 BYU), and there was another team on the periphery ready to slide in should somebody falter (No. 12 Texas Tech). That's great! It's late November, and there's a legitimate chance the Big 12 could get three teams in the field! If you'd have guaranteed Brett Yormark two teams before the season began, he'd have accepted the offer quicker than the AC Milan job.
But when you're seemingly on the cusp of having it all, that means you've a lot to lose.There are still two games left to play, plus a Big 12 Championship Game. A lot could go wrong, and this week presents an anxiety-producing set of circumstances.Utah, BYU and Texas Tech are all on the road as favorites of less than a touchdown. Utah is favored by 7 points against TCU, and that's the largest spread of the three. If you want to use math, the implied odds of the moneyline prices at DraftKings say there's only a 33.1% chance all three win this weekend. Thankfully, using the same math, there's only a 4.2% chance all three lose.
Still, one misstep could change the Big 12's overall picture. If it's BYU who falls while Tech and Utah win, the league is probably in a good spot, assuming both win next week. They'd be locked into the Big 12 Championship, and both would probably get in regardless of the result there.But if Tech loses, things could get more complicated. That could lead to a Big 12 Championship game where Utah faces a two-loss BYU or a two-loss Texas Tech. If Utah wins that game, how confident are you that a three-loss BYU or Texas Tech will hold on to a spot? Keep in mind the Red Raiders are 9-1 right now and wouldn't be in the field if the season were over.And there are other potential complications. The Big 12 has two other teams in the rankings with No. 19 Arizona and No. 20 Houston. Neither harbors delusions of making the playoffs at this point, but they're also on the road this week, and neither is favored by more than a touchdown. Should either lose, it would impact the resumes of the league's three playoff hopefuls. Both Tech and Utah have wins over Houston. All three have beaten Arizona. 
There's plenty to be nervous about in the Big 12 in Week 12. 2. TennesseePerhaps the committee will one day be forced to remember Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 earlier this year. They have not at this point, and Tennessee cannot afford to assume they ever will, so the best plan of attack for the Volunteers is to win their final two regular-season games to reach 10-2. It probably won't be enough to get to the SEC Championship or earn a first-round bye, but 10-2 would probably bring a home playoff game, and the Vols have been very tough to beat at Neyland Stadium this season.But timing is everything, and the timing of this weekend's game might make some Vols nervous. Old friend Lane Kiffin is coming to town, and while many years have passed since Kiffin left Knoxville in the dead of night, there are plenty of hard feelings remaining. Maybe not to the intensity of hurling golf balls and mustard bottles at him (which, seriously, don't do that), but hard feelings all the same.And Kiffin is coming to town with his back against the wall. LSU lost to Texas last week to knock itself out of playoff contention, and now Kiffin has had to spend the whole week listening to everybody talk about how LSU just lit a bunch of money on fire to be right back where they already were. He's heard about how Brian Kelly never lost four SEC games in a season (though he probably would have if, you know, they didn't fire him halfway through last season).
The best way for Lane to shut everybody up and make himself feel better? By going into Neyland Stadium and doing something nobody else, not even Alabama, has done this year: beat Tennessee.Could you imagine? What if Tennessee missed out on the CFP this season because it lost to Lane Kiffin. It's the kind of nightmare scenario that's surely keeping plenty of Vols up at night this week.3. The SECOh, don't worry, Tennessee isn't the only SEC team feeling it this week. Everybody is talking about how much the CFP loves the SEC and overrates it, and while there's certainly some truth to it, the biggest factor inflating SEC resumes is the strength of their schedules. I don't care which metric you use; they all agree on one thing: SEC teams have played tougher schedules than others.
That could change a bit this week, though, because it's what's lovingly referred to as "Cupcake Week" in the SEC. Yes, while every other league gets its FCS games out of the way early, some SEC teams hold on to the old tradition of saving them for November. I believe it's the smart way to do it. This week, No. 3 Alabama, No. 25 Ole Miss, Auburn and Mississippi State are all playing FCS opponents.What kind of impact will it have on their respective strengths of schedule? Will it hurt Alabama enough to get them out of those top four spots and put it within range of Tennessee should the Vols beat LSU? Then what happens?And what about all those 6-4 teams that are ranked at the bottom of the poll? South Carolina is a dog to Georgia. Missouri is a small favorite at home against Kentucky. What if all those 6-4 teams suddenly find themselves at 6-5? What happens to the SEC's SOS superiority then? 
The Missouri/Kentucky game is especially interesting. Right now Mizzou counts as a solid win for Georgia and Texas. If it loses to Kentucky, it'll be 6-5. Meanwhile, Kentucky is a solid win for Alabama and Tennessee. If it loses, it'll have lost three straight and may fall out of the top-25 entirely.This week's SEC slate could be far more consequential than many realize.4. PJ FleckIt's PJ Fleck's tenth season at Minnesota. The only times the Gophers have failed to make a bowl game during his tenure were his first season of 2017 when they finished 5-7, and the 2020 COVID season when they went 3-4. They've been to a bowl every other season, and they've won each and every single one of them.For a program like Minnesota, that kind of consistent success is one they're proud of. But as we head into Week 12, there's no guarantee the Gophers will keep the streak alive. They're small home dogs to Northwestern this weekend and will finish at rival Wisconsin next week. Neither of those two are in a great spot right now. Northwestern will be without its starting QB Aidan Chiles again, and Wisconsin, well, Wisconsin lost to Maryland last week.
The problem is Minnesota isn't exactly lighting it up right now, either. Fleck was crowdsurfing in the locker room after upsetting Iowa 13-10 in Week 8, but it's been three losses since. The OT losses to Indiana and UCLA were understandable. Both are likely playoff teams.But last week's 42-14 loss to Penn State was concerning. It was the kind of loss that makes you wonder what the mental state of this Gophers team is heading into the home stretch. A loss this weekend could make for a very tense Thanksgiving week ahead of that season finale against Wisconsin.5. Sonny DykesI mentioned earlier that TCU is a home underdog to Utah this weekend. I don't know that beating the Utes would be enough to save Sonny Dykes' job, but it certainly wouldn't hurt. On the flip side, a failure to reach a bowl game would almost certainly doom Dykes to the unemployment line, and he needs at least one more win in the final two games of the season.
The problem is if you don't win this week at home against a 10-0 Utah team, you'll be in a position where you have to win on the road next week at Texas Tech.It's not a great spot to be in! That trip to the national championship game feels like a very long time ago in Fort Worth.

Either way, his latest team should be No. 1 when the Associated Press Top 25 Poll updates Monday, especially after Houston blasted Kansas, 92-83, late Thursday in the title game of the Players Era 8 inside Michelob Ultra Arena out in Las Vegas.What. A. Performance.In a matchup with a Kansas outfit that entered undefeated and had beaten Kentucky by 20 just last week, the Cougars dominated. They led by as many as 24 points. They never trailed. They mostly cruised to a nine-point victory to improve to 6-0 with wins over Florida and Kansas, the schools currently ranked third and fourth at KenPom.com.

title: Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk' - CBS Sports
description: Wemby, once again, did something unusual and mesmerizing on Thursday by shooting a jumper at the rim
body:
Wemby, once again, did something unusual and mesmerizing on Thursday by shooting a jumper at the rim
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026

    9:44 am ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.Let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.
Officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.That begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention. 
Wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.Fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he said after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award. 
If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

title: Current's Croix Bethune focused on being 'me. M.E. -- Most Essential, version of yourself' ahead of NWSL final - CBS Sports

body:
Now starring for the Kansas City Current, the dynamic playmaker faces her former club, the Washington Spirit, in her third consecutive title game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:12 am ET

            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        WASHINGTON D.C. -- The 2026 NWSL Championship will feature two of the top clubs and some of the league's best players. One of them is 5-foot-3, has a deceptive left foot and just won her second midfielder of the year award in three seasons in the league.Croix Bethune, the 25-year-old attacking midfielder for the Kansas City Current, set a league record for most assists in a single season with 11 connections to her teammates. The previous record of 10, set in 2016 by former Portland Thorns FC player and U.S. women's national team hall of famer Tobin Heath, had stood for a decade. Bethune's efforts earned her a Best XI honor and the midfielder of the year award, and now she's experiencing her third NWSL Championship week in three years.  "Not my first rodeo, so, hopefully [we] end up on the brighter side of things this time. It's exciting. I mean, this is the end goal. This is where everyone wants to get, and now that we're here, we just have one more step to accomplish. Grateful to be in this position, especially with a new team. But yeah, we're still excited because this will be a great game," Bethune said of her return to the NWSL Championship with a new team.Bethune's NWSL arrivalAfter Bethune established her game at USC and the University of Georgia, where she had to overcome three ACL injuries and scored 30 goals with 28 assists over 65 matches, her entry into the league was met with excitement for her creativity and flair on the ball. Injury history aside, she was a player with raw talent who still had room for growth and development.She may have exceeded expectations in her first pro year. She won rookie of the year and midfielder of the year honors when she matched the single-season assist record in 17 games and scored five goals, but was unable to play in the 2024 NWSL Championship. Her season was cut short following a meniscus tear, and she rehabbed and returned in 2025; her two-assist, three-goal sophomore season took some getting used to, but she was still a factor in the playoffs, scoring in the semifinal and helping the Spirit reach another NWSL Championship.
Whether on the pitch or off the field, the way she shows her personality in interviews, on social media or in her choice of fashion apparel makes her unique and one of the league's rising stars.
"Yeah, I want people to know that they can be themselves and F what anybody has to say about them, whether it's good or bad, because it's your life and you're the only one with yourself 24/7, if that makes sense. From my [NWSL Awards] outfit, I'm creative. That's just how I express myself onto the playing field. And something that sticks with me, is me. M.E. -- Most Essential, version of yourself. Just always be you because you'll always be happy at the end of the day," she said after winning her 2026 awards.Returning to Audi FieldOn Saturday, Bethune will go up against her former club, the Washington Spirit, where she left a huge impact despite just two seasons of play. The Spirit drafted her third overall with a pick they traded up with Chicago Stars FC to get, and the move seemed to pay off quickly. The prospect of seeing Bethune evolve alongside Trinity Rodman or Sofia Cantore was short-lived after a trade to Kansas City Current ahead of the 2026 season.
But returning to Audi Field feels familiar and exciting for the player, despite the classic storyline of a former player returning ahead of a big game."Yeah, I mean DC is a great city. It's great to be back and great to be in the final with K.C. I think it'll be a very fun and interesting game. But the goal is to get to the final. So glad to make it back again," she said."For this team, we have worked so hard to get to this point. I feel like we started off pretty rocky in the beginning of the season. A lot of people probably counted us out. Like I said, who cares what people have to say? And I think that we make it count when you should make it count. And I think in the playoffs, in the end of the season, we definitely showed that with big-time wins."
Current chemistryYear one in Kansas City was another high bar for Bethune. Setting a single-season assist record is impressive on its own, but what has stood out is her ability to adapt quickly to a new environment and be a consistently productive player, even if there were some small stretches of nagging injuries along the way.She set up fellow attackers Temwa Chawinga and Michelle Cooper throughout the year. The trio hasn't always been able to be on the pitch at the same time, but when they are, they're on fire, and now all three are available when it counts the most."They make my job easy. They're technical. They have speed. They have soccer IQ. I think that we got in the groove of things pretty easily and very fast, and I think when you have people that understand the game, it's easier," she said.
"All of us not being on the field at the same time throughout the season, which is true, I think that's our biggest advantage during the final. Now, our entire team is healthy, our entire team, not our first 11, our entire team, but at times when we weren't together, some people have to show up. They have to step up a little more. But when we are, it's really tough for teams to figure out which player to stop because there's so much firepower."Her adaptability and relatability might be her special X-factor. A change of environment, a first year on a new team and a first-time NWSL coach proved to be not hurdles but challenges she turned into opportunities."It's funny coming in as a pro. I feel like I haven't just had one coach. I've gone through a couple of coaches in D.C. My first year, we had Adrian [Gonzalez], then we had Jona [Giraldez], and then we had Adrian. So it's not anything new to have a new coach for the first go around. Changes happen, adversity happens. Like, that's just something you have to adapt to, and I think I do pretty well at that," she said.
"Chris [Armas] is such a great guy. He's made it so easy, and it's been our little secret, kind of. But it's our little pact because I'm new to the team. He's new to the team. So, we're kind of in it together."Consistency leads to USWNT call-upsNo matter what happens in the NWSL Championship, Bethune's year isn't exactly over. She was recently named to the U.S. women's national team roster for the upcoming Concacaf W Championship. The tournament serves as qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup.She points to three big areas of growth, starting with maturity."When people hear Croix, they obviously think creative, flashy, flair. And as a younger player, I loved that, but that's not what gets the job done. So, I think being mature and getting the win while still having those moments. Two, I'd say consistency. I know Emma has mentioned that a couple of times. 'We want to see you be consistent,' which I definitely understand. So, I think that has improved, and also just adding more tricks to the bag ... Like I've been working on set pieces. And I think I've improved defensively as well, which has been something they really wanted," she said.
Bethune's goals for the year were plentiful; she's already checked off some. She says winning another midfielder award, returning to the postseason, making the championship final and even breaking the assist record were all on her list. Getting back in the mix with the national team was another, and now she'll be competing on one of the big rosters manager Emma Hayes put together."I feel like I've been working all year to get called into camps, especially this one. Being hurt and missing the October camp [against Spain] was very tough for me. So to see that they recognize the work that I'm putting in for this November camp, it means everything. Especially it being my first Concacaf Championship and Emma's, this is like a huge roster to make leading into World Cup," she said.How to watch Spirit vs. CurrentDate: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160

        Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity. In the Houston Texans' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011. Meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history. What surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Fernando Mendoza, Raiders upset Denver Broncos at Mile High as 10.5-point underdogs Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13. After adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos. Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Titans' Tony Pollard explodes for 200-plus scrimmage yards, multiple TDs in Cowboys homecomingTony Pollard is ascending to new heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans. Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving, and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey. 
Pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers. Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends. Tony Pollard last three games, Weeks 7-10*NFL RB rankRush yards27910thRush TD5T-1stReceiving Yards112T-9thReceiving TD1T-7thScrimmage TD6T-1st* On bye in Week 9
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jahmyr Gibbs rushes for 120-plus yards vs. Buccaneers No.1 run defenseDetroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFL's No. 1 run defense?The Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dolphins defy the odds, lose by just one score at 8-1 Buffalo BillsThe Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills, the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers. However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.How is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik. Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at theIndianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.No team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints sack Bears' Caleb Williams a season-high five timesChicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out. Williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the New Orleans Saints. Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the Minnesota Vikings' Andrew Van Ginkel (8.5) and Dallas Turner (8.0). The Saints' defense as a whole hasn't been stellar this season, profiling as the league's No. 25 scoring defense (26.2 points per game allowed), but they'll combine to sack Williams a season-high five times on Sunday. Williams' 3.35-second average time to throw is the longest in the NFL among the league's 31 qualified quarterbacks, which will doom him against Granderson, Young and the New Orleans defense.

title: Why having fun is non-negotiable for Trinity Rodman - CBS Sports
description: WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration
body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.
It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun."I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she said Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose."
Rodman at her peakFive years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around."I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah."Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.
"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'"The Spirit's silly sideThere's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit."I am excited to go in every day," Morgan said. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'"
The list of silly things is endless."We have these big red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls."Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable."I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman said. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many new players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable."
The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand."I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me."The NWSL's shining starKang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.
"Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone said. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele."Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship."Obviously, it was incredibly important for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL."
Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL."She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] New York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already."She's fun, she's engaging," Stone said. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity."
Rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation."Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity."How to watch Spirit vs. CurrentDate: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160

        Week 10 was not quite what we were hoping. After finishing the first half of the season above .500, we went 2-3 last week and are now 25-25 on the season.And it was agonizing. The Ravens failed to hit their OVER 20.5 points thanks to a drop at the 1-yard line and, later, a game-sealing fumble in Chargers territory. Los Angeles beat Baltimore 23-20. The hook got us. We were looking for 4+ receptions from Colby Parkinson, but he managed only two. And the Seahawks beat the Raiders but didn't pick off Fernando Mendoza.The wins were good ones. The 49ers covered at the Cowboys, and Josh Downs stepped right in and produced for the Chiefs, going well over the 25+ yard mark we had set for him. Let's not bite the hand that feeds us.Josh Downs 36+ receiving yards (-110)In his Kansas City debut, Josh Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown ... on eight routes run! In that teeny-tiny sample size, he provided exactly what the Chiefs had hoped: a man-coverage-beating slot presence who adds a little juice downfield, too. He should, at the very least, be able to put up those numbers again against a beatable Cardinals defense.
Lions cover (-7) vs. Buccaneers (-108)There simply aren't enough good things to say about the Buccaneers' defense. It is what's kept them afloat in an underwhelming NFC South; the Tampa Bay offense is scoring just 20.7 points per game, 22nd in the NFL.With uncertainty regarding Baker Mayfield's status, I just don't see a way for Jalon Daniels and co. to find much success here. The Buccaneers lead the NFL in yards per rush, but the Lions have been solid defending the ground game. The secondary has improved significantly, too, and ball-hawking safety Kerby Joseph is expected back this week. On the other side, the Lions should find some success, even if it's not up to their normal standard. Detroit is averaging 28.6 offensive points per game, the fifth-highest in the NFL, and when not pressured, Jared Goff is absolutely cooking—only Brock Purdy, Trevor Lawrence, and Joe Burrow have a higher expected points added per play. For all the good things Todd Bowles' defense does, it is 28th in pressure rate. Tony Pollard anytime touchdown (-125)Tony Pollard faces his former team and is on a hot streak, with six touchdowns in his last three games. The Cowboys, meanwhile, have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns to running backs, the fourth-most in the NFL, and five receiving touchdowns to running backs, tied for the most in the league. They just got burnt to a crisp by Christian McCaffrey in the passing game, too. Last week, Pollard caught eight of nine passes for 66 yards and a touchdown.
The Titans' offense is (obviously) not the 49ers' offense, but it should find enough success to get Pollard into the end zone at least once.J.J. McCarthy 1+ interceptions (-156)J.J. McCarthy has exceeded all expectations as the Giants starting quarterback after coming in midseason, playing far, far better than he did for any extended time with the Vikings. He has only two interceptions, but he has also had three would-be picks dropped and is one of the luckiest quarterbacks in that category.Meanwhile, the Jaguars have forced 12 interceptions this year, the third-most in the league, and they just added Jessie Bates III. I anticipate the Jacksonville offense will keep rolling, which will force McCarthy to chase the game all afternoon. That sounds like a recipe for at least one interception for me.
Bengals money line vs. Commanders AND Chase Brown anytime touchdown (+112)The Bengals are a top-tier Super Bowl contender. There's little doubt about that. The Commanders, meanwhile, are simply trying to hang around in the awful NFC East. I'd be really surprised if Washington finds a way to win this game; Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are simply too good against an up-and-down defense.It's been a tougher year for Chase Brown, but he's still a workhorse back in an offense that racks up points. He found the end zone twice last week, which should be a positive regression for him. Prior to that, he had just one score on 142 touches. This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
🏈 Five things to know Friday The Texans demolished the Colts on 'Thursday Night Football.' It took a week longer than some expected, but the effects of the Colts' trade deadline fire sale were on full display in a 26-3 drubbing. Houston had its way in all three phases. C.J. Stroud was excellent in another three-touchdown performance, Will Anderson Jr. sacked Daniel Jones for a safety and the Texans even blocked a field goal in a game that was never competitive. This could be the kind of get-right game that helps the Texans spark a late-season push to the postseason, and on the other side, this might not be the last time the Colts find themselves on the wrong end of a blowout as their campaign withers away.Puka Nacua and Marlon Humphrey face discipline. The Rams were already planning on being without Nacua for the next three games as he continues his injured reserve stint, but now he is also out due to the suspension the league handed down for a violation of the personal conduct policy. He can serve the suspension while on IR and will be eligible for reinstatement on Dec. 14. The Ravens, on the other hand, were not expecting to be without Humphrey in Week 11 until they sent him home from the facility and announced a one-game deactivation. Humphrey made disparaging remarks about the city of Baltimore, which drew immense backlash from throughout the community and forced the Ravens' hand.NBA trade buzz is already heating up. Trade season, in earnest, is still about a month away. But there has already been one in-season deal, and more could be on the horizon with the amount of chatter that is ongoing throughout the league. Dejounte Murray is at the center of the discussion since he requested a trade. Two teams reportedly emerged as potential destinations for the Pelicans guard, and Murray himself likes one of them as a preferred landing spot. Also, Kyrie Irving is said to be on the Jazz's radar, which makes little sense if you ask us. A couple of other players in demand: Anthony Davis and Trey Murphy III.The White Sox traded Luis Castillo to the Rockies. Speaking of trades, Chicago dealt a couple of pitchers in the wake of its Dustin May signing. Castillo and Davis Martin are headed to Colorado in exchange for Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz. It's a deal we can get behind for the Rockies, who are always in search of help on the mound. But for the White Sox? They receive a lower grade since they made an aggressive play to acquire Castillo just a few months ago at the trade deadline and are already done with him. Signings and trades will continue to fly in ahead of the lockout, so keep an eye on these teams who reportedly have their sights set on their next moves.The RJ Luis saga at LSU reached a boiling point. Just one day after the Tigers defied SEC rules and inserted Luis into action, the university decided this is a battle not worth fighting. LSU president Wade Rousse instructed coach Will Wade not to play Luis moving forward as the conference threatens retaliation, including the school's expulsion. It was a notable change of tune after the Tigers went all in to play the former St. John's star and NBA signee, who is ineligible under SEC rules but received a preliminary injunction that LSU said should allow him to play. If this is finally the end of Luis' attempts to suit up with the Tigers, the situation is a total failure for both him and LSU. 😔 Do not miss this: NBA's big disappointments so far 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            The NBA season started one month ago today. The first stanza of the campaign brought a great deal of excitement at the top of the league with superstars doing superstar things and most of the projected championship contenders getting off to hot starts. But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be. Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season. Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player: Gonzalez: "Through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his new four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome."Another major disappointment: The Kings. How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams.

You can be sure they will have their eyes on these five key matchups in Week 12. Another important clash is the only top-25 contest of the week: No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina. Fornelli: "Even though it's a night game at Williams-Brice Stadium, which is one of the more underrated environments in the sport, the Bulldogs just look like the best team in the country, and have for a while. Also, how fired up will South Carolina be for this game? Last week's loss ended any playoff hopes they had. If Georgia gets off to a good start, you can't ignore the possibility that Carolina just checks out of the game and Georgia steamrolls them. The Pick: Georgia -14.5 (-112) at DraftKings"Moving away from the SEC, look out for a potential upset in the Big Ten.                                                             This is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert, and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.
